title: Sensitivity bound for sums of angles
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, let $\ell\ge 0$ be an integer, and let $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_\ell\in\mathbb R$. The rotation sensitivity of $A$ at angle $\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\delta_j$ is at most $\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}s_A(\delta_j)$, where $s_A(u)$ denotes the rotation sensitivity at angle $u$.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. For any measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, integer $\ell\ge0$, and real angles $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_\ell$, $s_A(\sum_{j=1}^\ell\delta_j)\le\sum_{j=1}^\ell s_A(\delta_j)$.
